why_partial_not_ready: B1, B2, B3, B4 and P1 are all repaired and demonstrated, and the multi-positive CONFLICTING_AUTHORITY gap is CLOSED. The single reason this is not READY is HQ247-OPEN-001: decide() still leaks roughly 12 to 15 allocated blocks per call. The commission's READY status is not conditioned on the leak being closed in so many words, but returning READY over an open native memory defect I could not isolate would be the same dishonest green refused in every prior stage. The leak is precisely measured, not worse than base, and demonstrably does not affect decision correctness, replay identity, custody hash or parity.

repaired.B1: preserved and further stressed: 12 lie variants across list and tuple subclasses, on relations AND authority snapshots for Stage B; all refused by exact-type admission, no OOB, no silent truncation, no ownership violation. Standalone reproducer exits 0.
repaired.B2: PyObject_Call was passed the snapshot as the ARGS argument instead of a 1-tuple. Repaired with PyTuple_Pack(1, snapshot). This was the defect that made the genuine positive path unreachable.
repaired.B3: both PyErr_Fetch sites now fetch all three slots, NormalizeException all three, obtain the message via PyObject_Str with a defensive PyErr_Clear, and release pt, pv AND tb.
repaired.B4: non-str relation_kind and target_use are rejected with an exact typed integrity error before any PyUnicode_AsUTF8, in both decide and validate_decision_replay. 108 malformed inputs exercised standalone with no crash.
repaired.P1: effective_scope and directionality_or_symmetric are taken from the ADMITTED relation instead of being hardcoded to DISTINCT_BY_DEFAULT/SYMMETRIC. The by_key object key is now correct, which is what makes genuine AUTHORIZED reachable at all.
repaired.duplicate_suppression: the by_key adjacent-duplicate check now uses an owned C copy of the previous key instead of a borrowed pointer
repaired.source_ordering_block: the three parallel lists and the PyList_AsTuple handoff were rewritten as a single sorted pass with one explicitly-consumed tuple conversion. Honest note: this did NOT change the measured leak, which is itself part of the evidence that the parallel lists were not the cause.

closed_coverage_gap.how: a sibling relation is derived from the ACCEPTED fixture with its own relation_id, replay_identity and recomputed content_hash, so it is an individually valid independent receipt authorising the same exact relation key on its own. No authority forged, no decision function monkeypatched, trusted guard never bypassed.
branches_exercised: precedence first entry dominating three lower negatives
